page.layout: One page of running text, single column. Catchword "qui" at the lower right. No marginal notes. Faint show-through of the reverse page at the lower left, not transcribed.

main_text.p: hoc Cryptiæ tale tradit: principes juventutis per intervalla temporis validissimos & solertissimos ejus ætatis emisse solis pugionibus armatos, & cibi quantum satis erat secum ferentes: hos interdiu obscuris locis heic illic sparsos delituisse, noctu vero viis se committentes quosque Helotum deprehenderent, mastasse, sæpe etiam in agrum profectos robustissimos quosque eorum & valentissimos interemisse. Durarunt ephori in republica ad regnantem Cleomenem, qui libertate civitatis oppressa hos quoque e medio sustulit. Præter hos & reges cum senatu, alii quoque magistratus in republica Spartana fuère. Horum in numero Bidiæi erant, quos juniorum certaminibus præsediisse, & controversias eorum diremisse, & curiam in foro juxta regum senatusque & ephororum curias habuisse, ex Pausa-niâ dixi, pari numero cum ephoris, obscuri in historiis: & his etiam obscurio-res harmosyni, ab Hesychio tantum in lexico memorati, præfecti, ut idem ait, servando decenti mundo muliebri, ἀρχὴ τῆς ἐν Λακεδαίμονι ἐπὶ τῆς ἀ-[?] σωρίας [?] γυναικῶν [?], reprimendo scilicet exorbitanti fœminarum luxui in veste rebusque cæteris institutis:tum em-pedori, soli quoque Hesychio nominati, qui

page.notes: The Greek phrase is set inline and is only partly legible at the line break; the marked letters and the word beginning the second Greek line are doubtful. "instituti:tum" carries a colon as printed, possibly a misprint for "instituti: tum". The long s is rendered as plain s throughout, and "Pausa-nià" reads the printed s as s. The lower-left fragments are show-through from the reverse and were left out.
